task.description: WF-02 step 3 gate, SECURITY-REVIEWER, the first own-auth code of the product (read only; OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 V2, V3, V4, V5, V7, V8 as the checklist). Look hard at: scrypt parameters and the timing-safe compare; the dummy hash path for unknown/disabled accounts (one scrypt each, byte-equal answers); session cookie flags (__Host-, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite), session id entropy and hashing at rest, logout and password-change revocation; CSRF and Origin on session routes only; re-auth token one-time consumption in the same transaction; the setup token one-time use with timingSafeEqual; lockout and the admin delay under the per-row locks (no check-then-act); rate limits and the client address on Vercel (x-forwarded-for exactly one IP) and on Node (socket only); TOTP window, replay and recovery codes stored as HMAC; reset links; RLS forced and the tenant context set in the same transaction; grants.sql; the audit chain append in the same transaction and its refusals (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE); secrets: SECRET_PEPPER never logged, no secret in the repository, the uat-login secret file rules; error answers leak no stack, SQL or path; db-verify reads URLs from env only. Verify by reading AND by your own probes on a fresh clone of 2f267d1 under <scratch> (npm ci in app/; PGlite; app.request in-process; never the repository test suites, npm run check or e2e: decision 0110). PASS or FAIL with findings by severity, each with file:line and the exact change wanted. Be thorough. Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). A server you start binds port 0 or a free high port and is stopped by its exact process id; never bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790. One browser at a time on this PC. No git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. LF line endings. Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). items.Q7: applicable and met. Search of the change and of the page files (self_check S1): every match is a pinned action sha, an image digest, a CI address holding only $POSTGRES_PASSWORD, the SecLists commit sha, the seed audit hashes, the seed fake password hashes, or DUMMY_HASH (password.js:26, the hash of a discarded random text, not a secret); the page files hold only the old office checksums. SECRET_PEPPER is read only in config.js:118-133 (the refusal texts are fixed, without the value) and used only in keys.js; CI makes peppers at run time with ::add-mask::. Probes: no setup token, password, e-mail, client address, session token, CSRF token or pepper in any log line; log keys closed; session token, CSRF token, re-auth token, reset code, TOTP secret and recovery codes are not in the database in clear (HMAC or AES-GCM only); db-verify and uat-login output never echo an address, a password or a server text.
items.Q8: applicable and met for M2.2 (no tenant route exists; the organisation of a session comes from the membership row, readSession auth-store.js:36). Probes: under withTenant(A) orgs, org_members and invites show only A, B by id gives 0 rows, an update of B 0 rows, an insert into B is refused 42501; sai_app without settings sees 0 orgs; a forged non-uuid app.org_id errors and does not widen; audit_log is invisible to a tenant; the sai_app grants equal the design table exactly (no TRUNCATE, no DELETE on users, orgs, org_members, invites, audit_log); sai_preview, sai_app_login and PUBLIC hold no table grant; no public relation is owned by an app role. Admin routes: anonymous, random or malformed cookie and an ordinary session get a 404 byte-equal (body and headers) to an unknown /api path, with no row changed. Login of an unknown, disabled or deleted e-mail is byte-equal to a wrong password, one scrypt each; real-scrypt medians 539, 540, 542 ms (wrong, unknown, disabled).
items.Q9: applicable and met. No .query or .exec with a template literal or concatenation in app/server, app/api, app/scripts. Dynamic SQL only in db-verify.js:42-44 (identifiers from the catalog through format %I and quote_ident, values bound $1-$3) and in the old password step of migrate.js:60 (%L of a setting). grants.sql: static GRANTs inside if-blocks, no execute.
items.Q10: applicable and met (with the residual of finding F4). A DbError answers 503 db_unavailable or 500 server_error; a planted failing statement, a division by zero and a thrown Error holding a path and a secret-looking text all answer exactly {"error":"server_error"}, and the log line carries none of it; no pepper -> 503 server_config; an APP_ORIGIN that allows no cookie -> 503 server_config. Hostile input under 200 ms each: 64k ':' and '1.' to normalise, a 1 MB Cookie header, a 64k '@' e-mail, a 253-character e-mail x1000, a 64k text with a zero-width sign, a 30k-deep JSON; a __proto__ key -> bad_body; non-UTF-8 -> bad_json. uat-login: fetch with a 10 s timeout and redirect manual.

items.ASVS: V2: scrypt N=2^17 r=8 p=1, 16-byte salt, 64-byte key, full-length timingSafeEqual (password.js:65-73); 10-128 code points and the bundled common list; the dummy hash path; lockout 5 in 15 min for ordinary accounts and for e-mails without an active account, under a row lock; the admin never locked (probe: failed_logins 0) with the per-address delay; the re-auth counter separate (probe: 5 wrong -> 429 reauth_locked, failed_logins untouched); TOTP RFC 6238 with +-1 step and an atomic step claim (probes: t-2 refused, t+1 accepted, an older step after a newer one refused, a replay refused); recovery codes as HMAC, single use, case-insensitive. V3: __Host-sai_s; Path=/; Max-Age=604800; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Secure, no Domain (https probe); 32-byte token stored as HMAC; rotation at login (the old token dead); idle 12 h and absolute 7 d (probes at the boundaries); logout clears the cookie and kills the token; a password change kills every other session and their re-auth tokens; a reset kills every session; a repeated cookie reads as no session. V4: admin routes give the uniform 404 before any other check; the re-auth token is bound to user, session and purpose, single use (3 parallel uses -> one 200), expires at 5 min, and a thrown refusal after its consumption rolls it back. V5: strict schema (unknown key, type, length, invisible sign). V7: closed log keys. V8: no secret in the database or in answers beyond the masked fields of design 4.13.
items.CSRF_and_origin: met. On a session route: a missing Origin, 'null', a trailing slash, another port, localhost, upper case -> 403 origin_refused; text/plain, a form type, charset=latin1, 'application/json, text/plain', an extra parameter -> 415; a missing, one-character-off, shorter or longer x-sai-csrf and the CSRF token of another session -> 403 csrf_refused; the session stays alive after every refusal; login and setup need Origin; a login with a live session needs its CSRF token.
items.setup_token: met: sha256 digests compared by timingSafeEqual on 32 bytes (setup.js:16-34); wrong, 44-character, 42-character, empty and space-prefixed tokens answer the uniform 404 byte-equal; after setup_done the right token answers the uniform 404; the 6th setup call of an hour from one address -> 429 (seen when the probe first reused one address).
items.client_address: met: Node uses the socket only (11 logins with 11 spoofed X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP from one socket -> the 11th is 429, and the one rate key is mac(rl, login\0127.0.0.1)); Vercel uses x-forwarded-for only when it is exactly one IP literal (13 forms probed: a list, a port, a zone id, a leading zero, a name, too many groups, a double '::' -> null; ::ffff:v4 -> v4; IPv6 lower case); x-real-ip and x-vercel-forwarded-for are never read; no address -> the shared bucket 'unknown'.

findings.place: app/server/services/audit.js:152-173 (appendAudit), with the policy audit_log_select of app/db/migrations/0002_identity.sql:210-211
findings.item: Q8 / REQ-115 c10 (integrity of the audit chain)
findings.severity: MEDIUM, not blocking (not reachable in M2.2: every caller runs in the platform transaction)
findings.what: appendAudit works only in a platform transaction but does not enforce it. Under tenant settings (after switchToTenant, which the REQ-117 tenant routes will use) lastAuditHash reads no row, because the select policy gives rows to app.role 'platform' only; prev_hash becomes 64 zeros and the row is inserted anyway, so the chain breaks silently. Probe: withTenant(A, appendAudit(...)) then verifyAudit -> {ok:false, count:2, badId:'2'}.
findings.fix: In appendAudit, before lockChain, run one constant statement in audit-store.js, `select current_setting('app.role', true) as role`, and throw TypeError('audit: not a platform transaction') unless it is 'platform'; add the case to the audit-chain tests. REQ-117 then writes its audit rows before the switch, or the pipeline offers a platform-side audit step.

findings.place: app/server/http/rate-limit.js:35 (the key text), app/server/routes/auth.js:382 (the admin delay key), app/server/http/client-ip.js:44-52
findings.severity: MEDIUM, not blocking (the code follows REQ-114 'per IP' and the design; whether Vercel serves IPv6 clients today is not measured)
findings.what: An IPv6 client is keyed by its full /128 address. An attacker with an ordinary IPv6 /64 has 2^64 addresses, so the login limit (10 per 15 min), the reset and setup limits and the admin delay (the only brute-force brake on the never-locked admin account) do not hold against him. Ordinary accounts keep their per-account lock.
findings.fix: Key IPv6 addresses by their /64 prefix (the first four groups after expanding '::') for the labels rl and delay (ip_hmac may keep the full address), with a test where two addresses of one /64 share a bucket; or record in decisions/0137 that /128 keys are accepted, with the reason.

findings.what: The checks use lstatSync(file) and the read uses readFileSync(file), which follows a link: a file swapped for a symbolic link between the two calls is read (time of check versus time of use). Needs local write access to the folder of the secret file.
findings.fix: Open once with fs.openSync(file, fs.constants.O_RDONLY | fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW), run fstatSync on that descriptor for isFile and the mode, and read from the same descriptor.

findings.place: app/server/db/pg.js:26-34 (pool max 3), with the scrypt inside the request transaction (app/server/routes/auth.js:317, 358, 409; design 4.9.5)
findings.item: Q10 (one request does not break the work of others)
findings.severity: LOW (a residual of the accepted design shape)
findings.what: Each login holds one of the 3 pool connections of an instance for its whole scrypt (about 0.5 s, more under CPU load). Anonymous login attempts from a few addresses can keep the pool busy, so the other requests of that instance wait for a connection and answer 503 at the 4 s deadline. The design names the CPU bound (about 7 parallel logins) but not the pool bound.
findings.fix: Name the bound in the design residuals, or raise max for the function and measure it in the post-deploy record; no code change is needed for M2.2.

findings.what: A password change does not void an unused admin-issued reset code of the same user: the 30-minute link still sets a new password after the user changed his own.
findings.fix: Call deleteUnusedResets(req.q, row.id) (app/server/db/auth-store.js:527) in the password-change transaction.

Row-lock races, the COMMIT limit and RLS and grants on real Postgres 17 are proven here by reading only; the pg and migration-rehearsal jobs on GitHub must prove them (no CI run of 2f267d1 exists yet).
